_doc: Point-in-time retrospective. Every input was public on as_of; see sources. Hindsight lives only in outcome.json.
methodology: house v2 (EPP-distance adjustment), 6-section format; retro method r2: scenario inputs derived from dated facts by frozen rules (retro/README.md); electric utility signals

pit_profile.why: The Southern Company: 'Southern Company owns all of the outstanding common stock of Alabama Power, Georgia Power, Gulf Power, and Mississippi Power, each of which is an operating public utility company. The traditional operating companies supply electric service in the states of Alabama, Georgia, Florida, and Mississippi.'; among its risk factors, 'Southern Company and its subsidiaries are subject to substantial governmental regulation.', 'The operating results of Southern Company, the traditional operating companies, and Southern Power are affected by weather conditions and may fluctuate on a seasonal and quarterly basis.' and 'The costs of compliance with current and future environmental laws, including laws and regulations designed to address air quality, water, CCR, global climate change, and other matters and the incurrence of environmental liabilities could negatively impact the net income, cash flows, and financial condition of Southern Company, the traditional operating companies, and/or Southern Power.' (its own FY2015 10-K); ENERGY_TRANSITION is live (from 2015-12-12): the company owns coal and lignite reserves and its CO2 risk factor puts the theme on the watch list, company-acknowledged, with no dated evidence that the market prices it for Southern Company

theme_watch.reason: Live: Southern Company's own FY2015 10-K says 'Alabama Power owns coal reserves near its Plant Gorgas and uses the output of coal from the reserves in its generating plants. Mississippi Power owns a lignite mine and equipment and has acquired and will continue to acquire mineral reserves located around the Kemper IGCC site in Kemper County.' and, of the EPA's CO2 rules for fossil fuel-fired units, 'The proposed guidelines and standards could result in operational restrictions and material compliance costs, including capital expenditures, which could affect future unit retirement and replacement decisions.' The stock trades at 16.2x FY16E — near its own median. Re-file as DISRUPTION_EXPOSED (ENERGY_TRANSITION) only if dated evidence shows the market pricing decarbonisation of Southern Company's coal reserves and the units they supply specifically.

BEAR.desc: EPS -2.1%/yr (worst year FY06-FY15, capped at 0%); P/E to its 10th pct

BASE.desc: EPS +13.8%/yr (Q3 revenue + margin + buyback); P/E at its 10-yr median

BULL.desc: EPS +13.8%/yr (FY06-FY15 CAGR); P/E holds its 75th pct

XBULL.desc: EPS +13.8%/yr (best 2-yr run FY06-FY15); P/E at its 90th pct

summary: SO (retrospective, 2016-12-02) ◉ BUY — Ratio B 0.51x (16.6% downside to Bear $39 / +32.6% upside to Bull $62) | Adj composite 3.36 vs market 3.18: gap +0.18 [FAIRLY VALUED] | +16% above the EPP floor $40 (14x FY16E $2.89) | Conservative 2-yr case: +25.7% total (+12.9%/yr) | At 16.2x FY16E the 15% hurdle price $62 sits between the BASE and BULL cases; retail kWh sales +3.2% in Q3 2016, forward revenues +16% (no Q4 2016 revenue guide, Q3 2016 revenue as reported); the energy transition is live and company-acknowledged; no dated evidence ties the multiple to it.
